L893: ## Verify the managed setting
L894: 
L895: After the app restarts, verify the policy from an affected user’s device:
L896: 
L897:   1. Sign in to the ChatGPT desktop app with an account covered by the policy.
L898:   2. Open Settings > General.
L899:   3. Find In-app updates and confirm that it shows Managed and the message “Your organization has turned off in-app updates.”
L900:   4. Confirm that your device management platform can still deploy an approved app version.
L901: The Check for Updates menu option can remain visible even when the policy blocks in-app updates. Use the Managed indicator to verify the policy instead of checking whether that menu option appears.
L902: 
L903: If the indicator doesn’t appear after the first restart, the app might still use a cached policy. Allow the policy to refresh, then fully quit and reopen the app again. Don’t rely on the update restriction until Managed appears.
L904: ## Deploy approved app versions
L905: 
L906: After you turn off in-app updates, use your existing device management process to deliver new releases:
L907:   1. Choose an app version that your organization plans to deploy.
L908:   2. Get the supported installation package for each operating system and device architecture in your fleet.
L909:   3. Test the release with a small group of representative users.
L910:   4. Deploy the approved package through Microsoft Intune, your MDM platform, or another software-deployment tool.
L911:   5. Check device inventory to confirm your platform installed the intended version, then expand the rollout to other groups.
L912: Your management platform determines how you stage releases, select versions, and recover when a deployment doesn’t complete. If your platform permits rollback, returning to an older version doesn’t extend support or guarantee service compatibility.
L913: 
L914: For macOS, download the cite475†ChatGPT desktop app installer†persistent.oaistatic.com . For Windows installation methods and architecture-specific packages, see cite410†Deploy the Windows app .

L870: ### Scheduled tasks create many worktrees
L871: 
L872: Frequent scheduled tasks can create many worktrees over time. Archive scheduled runs you no longer need and avoid pinning runs unless you intend to keep their worktrees.
L873: 
L874: ### Recover a prompt after selecting the wrong target
L875: 
L876: If you started a chat with the wrong target (Local, Worktree, or Cloud) by accident, you can cancel the current run and recover your previous prompt by pressing the up arrow key in the composer.
L877: ### Feature is working in the Codex CLI but not in the ChatGPT desktop app
L878: 
L879: The ChatGPT desktop app and Codex CLI can include different Codex versions, so features may reach one surface before the other. Experimental features might also land in Codex CLI first.
L880: 
L881: To get the version of the Codex CLI on your system run:
L882: 
L883:     `codex --version`
L884: To get the version of Codex bundled with your ChatGPT desktop app, use the retained `Codex.app` compatibility bundle path:
L885: 
L886:     `/Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/codex --version`
L887: ## Feedback and logs
L888: 
L889: Type `/` into the message composer to provide feedback for the team. If you trigger feedback in an existing chat, you can choose to share the existing session along with your feedback. After submitting your feedback, you’ll receive a session ID that you can share with the team.
L890: 
L891: To report an issue:
L892: 
L893:   1. Find cite476†existing issues†github.com on the Codex GitHub repo.
L894:   2. cite477†Open a new GitHub issue†github.com L895: 
L896: More logs are available in the following locations:
L897:   * App logs (macOS): `~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/YYYY/MM/DD`
L898:   * Session transcripts: `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` (default: `~/.codex/sessions`)
L899:   * Archived sessions: `$CODEX_HOME/archived_sessions` (default: `~/.codex/archived_sessions`)
L900: 
L901: If you share logs, review them first to confirm they don’t contain sensitive information.
L902: ## Stuck states and recovery patterns
L903: 
L904: If a chat appears stuck:
L905: 
L906:   1. Check whether Codex is waiting for an approval.
L907:   2. Open the terminal and run a basic command like `git status`.
L908:   3. Start a new chat with a smaller, more focused prompt.
L909: 
L910: If you cancel worktree creation by mistake and lose your prompt, press the up arrow key in the composer to recover it.
L911: ## Terminal issues
L912: 
L913: Terminal appears stuck
L914: 
L915:   1. Close the terminal panel.
L916:   2. Reopen it with `Ctrl`+```.
L917:   3. Re-run a basic command like `pwd` or `git status`.
L918: 
L919: If commands behave differently than expected, validate the current directory and branch in the terminal first.
L920: 
L921: If it continues to be stuck, wait until your active chats are complete and restart the app.

L1470: ## Command details
L1471: ### `codex` (interactive)
L1472: 
L1473: Running `codex` with no subcommand launches the interactive terminal UI (TUI). The agent accepts the global flags above plus image attachments. Web search defaults to cached mode; use `--search` to switch to live browsing. For low-friction local work, use `--sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval on-request`.
L1474: Use `--remote ws://host:port` or `--remote wss://host:port` to connect the TUI to an app server started with `codex app-server --listen ws://IP:PORT`. For a local Unix socket, use `--remote unix://` for the default socket or `--remote unix://PATH` for an explicit path. Add `--remote-auth-token-env <ENV_VAR>` when the server requires a bearer token for WebSocket authentication.
L1475: ### `codex app-server`
L1476: 
L1477: Launch the Codex app server locally. This is primarily for development and debugging and may change without notice.
L1478: 
L1479: [Input: Filter by key, type, or details]
L1480: Key  | Type / Values  | Details
L1481: --- | --- | ---
L1482: `--analytics-default-enabled`  | `boolean`  | Defaults analytics to enabled for first-party app-server clients unless the user opts out in config.
L1483: `--code-mode-host`  | `ws://HOST/PATH | wss://HOST/PATH`  | Connect to a remote Code Mode host instead of starting a local host. This outbound connection is shared across threads and is separate from `--listen`; use `wss://` for remote hosts.

L3303: ### `codex update`
L3304: 
L3305: Check for and apply a Codex CLI update when the installed release supports self-update. Debug builds print a message telling you to install a release build instead.
L3306: ## Flag combinations and safety tips
L3307: 
L3308:   * Use `--sandbox workspace-write` for unattended local work that can stay inside the workspace, and avoid `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` unless you are inside a dedicated sandbox VM.
L3309:   * When you need to grant Codex write access to more directories, prefer `--add-dir` rather than forcing `--sandbox danger-full-access`.
L3310:   * Pair `--json` with `--output-last-message` in CI to capture machine-readable progress and a final natural-language summary.
L3311: ## Interactive shortcuts
L3312:   * Type `@` to search for a file in the workspace and add its path to the prompt.
L3313:   * Press `Up` or `Down` to restore draft history.
L3314:   * Press `Ctrl`+`R` to search prompt history, then press `Enter` to use a match or `Esc` to cancel.
L3315:   * Press `Ctrl`+`O` or run `/copy` to copy the latest completed Codex output.
L3316:   * Prefix a line with `!` to run a local shell command under the current approval and sandbox settings.
findings: Official troubleshooting distinguishes standalone CLI from app-bundled Codex and gives separate version-check commands.
Official command reference documents codex update only when the installed release supports self-update; debug builds need a release install.
Official app-update administration guide confirms Check for Updates can remain visible while managed policy blocks updates. A visible menu alone does not prove update success.
limits: App-bundled command reports Codex binary version, not necessarily the desktop application build number researchers specify.
No universal consumer desktop version menu route verified from these pages.
